editor_note: Entry 8 renders "dynamical decoupling" as "desacoplamiento dinámico". That is the standard Spanish term, and it keeps the link URL and anchor unchanged.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The numbers and caveats all match the English: 1000 randomizations, about 11,000 circuit instances, 26.8 million instructions per qubit applied per job, batches=4, and the note that a supplied estimator_options replaces the defaults rather than merging with them. There is one gender-agreement error: [49] says "de baja entrelazamiento", but "entrelazamiento" is masculine, so it should be "de bajo entrelazamiento". There are also two stiff calques: "cómo contar contra ellos" in [60] and "es clásico en lugar de en el QPU" in [66]. Terminology is consistent: hamiltoniano, ansatz, twirling de puertas, desacoplamiento dinámico, shots, and backend falso for "fake".

The meaning is faithful throughout: the benchmark figures (44% vs 95.3%, the 26/60/70-qubit configurations), the caveats that the techniques are "not universally beneficial" and that results depend on the hardware, and the "lower is better" notes all survive. editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 1, 11 and 132 are faithful, and "ansatz", "puertas" and "parámetros variacionales" are used correctly and consistently. Entry 67 has two small losses and a register problem. "Much more than just the lowest energy eigenvalue" became "más que solo", which weakens the claim a little. "Thus" was dropped, so the text no longer says that the extra output is why Estimator is placed inside a cost function. It also uses the formal "Puede obtener" twice where the house convention is "tú". Entry 24 has a redundant calque, "La palabra 'ansatz' es una palabra alemana".

editor_note: The meaning is correct throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. One calque in the Credly privacy notice [12] needs fixing: "de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM" copies the English "consistent with". examples.why: The serial comma before 'y' is copied from English. Spanish does not use a comma before 'y' in a simple list.

editor_note: The page is faithful and reads naturally: "computación cuántica a escala de utilidad" is used consistently, "event replay course" becomes "basado en un evento grabado", and the informal register is kept. The one change I'd make is in entry [4]: "very similar to work published" became "comparable con un trabajo publicado", which drops the "very" and makes the claim weaker, and "comparable a" would be the more idiomatic preposition. "muy similar al trabajo publicado" is closer to the English. It doesn't mislead a learner.

examples.source: The result is very similar to work published on the cover of Nature in June 2023.
examples.translation: El resultado es comparable con un trabajo publicado en la portada de Nature en junio de 2023.
examples.suggested: El resultado es muy similar al trabajo publicado en la portada de Nature en junio de 2023.
examples.why: "comparable con" drops the "very" in "very similar", which makes the claim weaker, and "comparable a" is the more idiomatic preposition. It's a small change and doesn't mislead.

editor_note: Entry 82 matches the English and reads naturally: "Puedes configurar las opciones de supresión de errores en Sampler V2. Consulta la guía [Gestión de ruido del Sampler]…" keeps the tú register, the term "supresión de errores" matches the Strategy 3 heading (entry 81), and both references are kept.

None of the six rewritten entries (7, 21, 38, 45, 47, 58) would mislead a learner. They keep the meaning, and the key terms are right: "barrido de parámetros", "valores esperados", "disposición de qubits", "límite clásico de ±2". A native editor would still fix two small things. In entry 58, "curvas en negrita" borrows a typography word for plotted lines, and "curvas gruesas" or "más marcadas" is more natural. In entry 45, the same concept appears as "sistema objetivo" in the first sentence and as the English "target" in the second ("transpilamos para el target del simulador").

examples.source: the bold curves are their mean across the device
examples.translation: las curvas en negrita son su media en todo el dispositivo
examples.suggested: las curvas gruesas representan su media en todo el dispositivo
examples.why: 'Negrita' refers to bold type in text. For lines on a plot, Spanish technical writing uses 'gruesas', 'más marcadas' or 'de trazo grueso'.

examples.source: transpile against the simulator's target so the same pass manager is exercised end-to-end
examples.translation: transpilamos para el target del simulador, de modo que el mismo gestor de pases se pruebe de principio a fin
examples.suggested: transpilamos para el target (sistema objetivo) del simulador, de modo que el mismo gestor de pases se pruebe de principio a fin
examples.why: The previous sentence of the same entry says 'sistema objetivo', and this one switches to the English 'target' without linking the two. That is defensible because the Qiskit API object is called Target, but a gloss would keep the wording consistent.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The MIS constraints ("como máximo se seleccione uno de los extremos"), the clique and slack-variable reduction, and the fixed-angle QAOA with "arranque en caliente iterativo" all match the English, and the register is consistently "tú". Two wording slips are worth fixing. In [4], "Qiskit Functions es una función experimental" uses "función" for "feature", so the sentence reads "Functions is a function" (subject-verb agreement is also off). In [87], "all function features" became "todas las funciones", which turns the function's features into multiple functions.

examples.source: Qiskit Functions are an experimental feature available only to IBM Quantum® Premium Plan...
examples.translation: Qiskit Functions es una función experimental disponible únicamente para...
examples.suggested: Qiskit Functions son una funcionalidad experimental disponible únicamente para...
examples.why: Here 'feature' is translated as 'función', which clashes with the product name (Functions) and reads as 'Functions is a function'. 'Funcionalidad' avoids the clash, and the plural verb fits the plural name.

examples.source: for a detailed walkthrough of all function features
examples.translation: para un recorrido detallado por todas las funciones
examples.suggested: para un recorrido detallado por todas las características de la función
examples.why: 'Features of the function' became 'all the functions', which suggests several functions when the guide covers one function's features. The slip is small and would not mislead in context.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 39 is faithful and natural: "problema de muestreo adecuado para la ejecución con la primitiva SamplerV2" and "usamos StatevectorSampler de qiskit.primitives para la simulación local" keep both claims and match the file's feminine "la primitiva Sampler" convention (entries 9, 15).

All seven rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally, e.g. "sabiendo que no se producen falsos positivos" (entry 14), "Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada" (entry 20) and "kernels cuánticos proyectados" (entry 34), with "Hamiltoniano" kept consistent with entries 16/30/52.

All three rewritten entries are faithful and use tú. Entry 38 keeps the odd/even distance condition intact ("Si la distancia es impar, primero aplicamos un CNOT… Para una distancia par… después"), and entry 48 renders "expectation values" as "valores esperados" and "stabilizers" as "estabilizadores", matching the rest of the file.

Rewritten entry 9 is faithful and natural: "Usar la primitiva Estimator para calcular valores esperados de un observable" keeps Estimator in English and matches the page's existing "valores esperados" (entries 1, 18).

The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The physics passages keep the source's meaning: frustration, extensive energy, variance scaling with N, the NP-hard ground state and the solution/metadata description. Terms are used consistently (espín, Hamiltoniano, estado fundamental, vidrios de espín, transpilación, backend, job), and the informal tú register holds. A native editor would still fix two things. Entry [9] repeats "forma" ("completamente de forma local en una forma que pueda interactuar"). "Interaction/coupling strengths" is rendered as "fuerzas de interacción/acoplamiento" in [12], [16] and [44], where "intensidades" is the more idiomatic physics term.

examples.source: to formulate the problem entirely locally in a form that can interface with the Parity Twine Optimizer
examples.translation: para formular el problema completamente de forma local en una forma que pueda interactuar con el Parity Twine Optimizer
examples.suggested: para formular el problema de manera totalmente local, en un formato compatible con el Parity Twine Optimizer
examples.why: The repeated 'forma ... una forma' is clumsy translationese, and 'interactuar' is a literal calque of 'interface'.

examples.source: interaction strengths $J_ij$ between spins are randomly distributed
examples.translation: las fuerzas de interacción $J_ij$ entre espines se distribuyen aleatoriamente
examples.suggested: las intensidades de interacción $J_ij$ entre espines se distribuyen aleatoriamente
examples.why: 'Strength' here means coupling magnitude, not force. 'Intensidad de acoplamiento/interacción' is the conventional Spanish term. The meaning is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: None of the 12 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The central PNA explanation in [19] and [22] is faithful: noise channels are modeled after ideal gates, the inverses are propagated forward and absorbed into the observable, measuring \tilde{O} on the noisy circuit matches O on an ideal circuit, and sampling overhead is avoided. Three small editorial problems remain. [104] spells 'post-selección' with a hyphen, but [144]/[151]/[153] use 'postselección'; the unhyphenated form is standard. [155] translates the linked title as 'Combina las opciones...', while [13] translates the same title as 'Combinar opciones...'. [88] renders 'left-dressed' as 'se absorben por la izquierda', which interprets the term rather than translating it; the English gloss in parentheses keeps it recognizable.

examples.source: Enables edge-based post-selection using `rx` gates
examples.translation: Habilita la post-selección basada en aristas usando puertas `rx`
examples.suggested: Habilita la postselección basada en aristas usando puertas `rx`
examples.why: The spelling does not match 'postselección' in [144], [151] and [153]. Without the hyphen is the standard Spanish form.

examples.source: [Combine error mitigation options with the Estimator primitive]
examples.translation: [Combina las opciones de mitigación de errores con la primitiva Estimator]
examples.suggested: [Combinar opciones de mitigación de errores con la primitiva Estimator]
examples.why: [13] translates the same linked tutorial title differently. The title should be identical in both places.

examples.source: Single-qubit gates are left-dressed within the boxes.
examples.translation: Las puertas de un solo qubit se absorben por la izquierda (left-dressed) dentro de las cajas.
examples.suggested: Las puertas de un solo qubit se incorporan como 'dressing' por la izquierda (left-dressed) dentro de las cajas.
examples.why: 'Se absorben' interprets the Samplomatic dressing concept rather than translating it. It is not misleading, but it is loose, and the file already uses 'absorber' for PNA's own observable absorption.

editor_note: Entry 15 is faithful and reads naturally. "planificación de rutas de entrega para reducir el uso de combustible", "hamiltoniano de costo", "soluciones candidatas con QAOA" and the closing caveat about needing "un objetivo y restricciones que representen la aplicación prevista" all keep the English meaning, and "costo" matches the rest of the file. The lowercase "hamiltoniano" is the correct Spanish form, so it is not a defect even though other entries capitalize it.

I found no meaning errors: the kernel definition, the coset setup and the O(N^2) / N(N+1)/2 scaling argument all match the English. Two entries slip into the formal usted register ("Construya" in [0], "Su tiempo de ejecución" in [4]), while the rest of the page uses tú ("asegúrate", "consulta", "Calcula"). "Shot noise" is calqued as "ruido de disparo" in [24], where Spanish usually says "ruido de muestreo". [36] has two calques, "Ejercitamos este paso" and "se transpila contra una QPU", and [28] opens with "Nota que", where "Observa que" reads more naturally.

examples.source: Build a Qiskit pattern for evaluating entries into a quantum kernel matrix
examples.translation: Construya un patrón de Qiskit para evaluar entradas
examples.suggested: Construye un patrón de Qiskit para evaluar entradas
examples.why: This is the formal usted imperative; the page's convention is informal tú.

examples.source: Your runtime might vary.
examples.translation: Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.suggested: Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.why: Formal possessive, which breaks the tú convention used everywhere else on the page.

examples.source: exact (up to shot noise)
examples.translation: exacto (hasta el ruido de disparo)
examples.suggested: exacto (salvo el ruido de muestreo)
examples.why: 'Ruido de disparo' is a literal calque of 'shot noise'. The usual Spanish terms are 'ruido de muestreo' or 'ruido de shots', and 'salvo' conveys 'up to' better than 'hasta'.

examples.source: We exercise this step in the hardware example below, where the circuit is transpiled against a real QPU
examples.translation: Ejercitamos este paso en el ejemplo de hardware a continuación, donde el circuito se transpila contra una QPU real
examples.suggested: Aplicamos este paso en el ejemplo de hardware más adelante, donde el circuito se transpila para una QPU real
examples.why: 'Ejercitamos' and 'transpila contra' copy the English wording; a native technical writer would use 'aplicamos' and 'para'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The Krylov/Trotter explanation, the sparsity argument in [29] and the upper-bound caveat in [61] all keep their conditions and qualifiers, and core terms are consistent (hamiltoniano, compuerta, estado fundamental, transpilar). A native editor would still fix a few surface slips. The same linked tutorial title is given two ways, "hamiltoniano de química" in [10] and "hamiltoniano químico" in [15]/[36]/[66], and the addon is called both "complemento SQD de Qiskit" and "SQD Qiskit addon". There are also some small grammar and word choices to change: "de uno y dos partículas" should be "de una y dos partículas", "cota superior a" should be "cota superior de", "Prerequisitos" should be "Requisitos previos" or "Prerrequisitos", and "al que puedes referirte" is a calque. "Hopping" and "on-site" are left untranslated in [23].

examples.source: one- and two-particle reduced density matrices
examples.translation: matrices de densidad reducida de uno y dos partículas
examples.suggested: matrices de densidad reducidas de una y dos partículas
examples.why: Gender agreement error with 'partícula'. 'Cota superior a' is also a calque; 'cota superior de la energía' reads naturally.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization of a chemistry Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras de un hamiltoniano de química
examples.suggested: Diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras de un hamiltoniano químico
examples.why: The same tutorial title is rendered 'hamiltoniano químico' in [15], [36] and [66], so the link text is inconsistent.

examples.source: SQD Qiskit addon v0.11 or later
examples.translation: SQD Qiskit addon v0.11 o posterior
examples.suggested: Complemento SQD de Qiskit v0.11 o posterior
examples.why: [6] and [66] translate the addon as 'complemento SQD', so it is named inconsistently.

examples.source: Prerequisites
examples.translation: Prerequisitos
examples.suggested: Requisitos previos
examples.why: The standard spelling is 'prerrequisitos' (with double r), and technical docs usually prefer 'Requisitos previos'.

examples.source: which can be referred to for more details
examples.translation: al que puedes referirte para obtener más detalles
examples.suggested: que puedes consultar para obtener más detalles
examples.why: 'Referirse a' here calques the English 'refer to'. 'Consultar' is the idiomatic verb and is already used in [47].

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: entry 5 keeps the caveat with informal "Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar" and "Estimación de uso: 24 minutos en un procesador Heron r2", and entry 6 renders "Background" as "Contexto", a standard choice.

The meaning holds throughout, including the harder parts: the gamma curves falling toward 1.0, postselection rate against shot budget, and the caveat that the hardware estimate is coarser. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Some wording is still unidiomatic. "Bare" payload/circuit is rendered "sin procesar" ("unprocessed") in [58], [63], [73] and [76], where it actually means "without checks". "Commit" is calqued as "confirmar" (e.g. "confirma las mejores en el circuito"). The file mostly writes "qubit" but switches to "cúbit a cúbit" in [55], and "40,000 / 1,200" in [71] use English thousands separators.

examples.source: Sample the bare payload and the checked circuits with Qiskit Aer.
examples.translation: Muestrea el payload sin procesar y los circuitos comprobados con Qiskit Aer.
examples.suggested: Muestrea el payload sin comprobaciones y los circuitos comprobados con Qiskit Aer.
examples.why: 'Bare' here means 'without checks', but 'sin procesar' suggests the circuit has not been processed or transpiled. The same rendering appears in [63], [73] and [76].

examples.source: The package scores candidate checks against a noise model and commits the best ones to the circuit.
examples.translation: El paquete puntúa las comprobaciones candidatas frente a un modelo de ruido y confirma las mejores en el circuito.
examples.suggested: El paquete puntúa las comprobaciones candidatas frente a un modelo de ruido e incorpora de forma definitiva las mejores al circuito.
examples.why: 'Confirmar ... en el circuito' is a calque of 'commit' and reads unnaturally. It recurs in [57], [66] and [76].

examples.source: Each stabilizer is generally not qubit-wise commuting with the others
examples.translation: Cada estabilizador generalmente no conmuta cúbit a cúbit con los demás
examples.suggested: Cada estabilizador generalmente no conmuta qubit a qubit con los demás
examples.why: Everywhere else the file uses 'qubit'; 'cúbit' appears only here.

examples.source: at a 3% rate, 40,000 shots leave roughly 1,200 postselected samples per circuit
examples.translation: a una tasa del 3%, 40,000 shots dejan aproximadamente 1,200 muestras postseleccionadas por circuito
examples.suggested: a una tasa del 3 %, 40 000 shots dejan aproximadamente 1200 muestras postseleccionadas por circuito
examples.why: Many Spanish readers use the comma as a decimal separator, so '40,000' could be read as 40.
